answers.hint: Send { "answers": { "name": "milo", … } }. Every step you leave out takes its default, exactly as `init --yes` does with flags; GET /v1/provision lists them.

additionalProperties.hint: Answers arrive as strings from the terminal and from here, and are validated per step. Send the value as a string — including a boolean-looking choice, whose values are named in GET /v1/provision.

template.hint: Send the template's name as a string. GET /v1/templates lists what this server has.
template.description: Create the agent from a template in this server's sandbox instead of from answers. Needs `name`; takes `vars`.

name.description: The new agent's name, with `template`. Its slug becomes the id; the template sees both as {{agent.name}} and {{agent.id}}.

vars.hint: Send { "vars": { "store": "Acme" } }, every value a string. GET /v1/templates lists each template's variables.
vars.description: Values for the template's declared variables. A secret variable's value goes to the agent's .env and is never returned.

post.summary: Start a turn. Returns once accepted; the turn runs detached.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: 1-255 printable ASCII characters unique to this logical message. A retry with the same key and the same text and session answers 200 with the original turn (`replayed: true`) and runs nothing; with different text it is a 409. Remembered for 24 hours.

200.description: a replay of an Idempotency-Key already used for this message: the original turn, `replayed: true`

202.description: accepted: `{turnId, sessionKey}`, or with `stream: true` an event stream whose first frame is that object

schema.description: Server-sent events. Each frame's `data` is one event; the event table is in the wire spec (docs/04-SPEC-WIRE.md).

text.hint: Send { "text": "..." }. An empty turn would be billed for a full prompt and produce nothing.
text.description: What to say to the agent.

sessionKey.description: Which conversation this belongs to. Defaults to `api:default`.

role.hint: Name a role declared under model: in the manifest (GET /v1/agents/:id/config lists them), or omit role to run on main. A person adds one with PATCH /config path model.<name>.
role.description: A model role to run this turn on instead of main: one declared under `model:`, as a schedule names one with `role:`. This turn only; the conversation's other turns are unaffected. Refused before the turn starts when no such role is declared.

runtimeNote.hint: Send runtimeNote as non-empty text of at most 8000 characters: the active project, today's date in the person's zone, an attachment's extracted text.
runtimeNote.description: Your application's note about this message: shown to the model in its own block before the text, labelled as not written by the person, for this turn only. Kept on the turn record (`GET …/turns`), never in history. Refused when `from` is an agent.

peerAsk.hint: Send { "peerAsk": { "askedBy": "<silo>/<agent>" } }, naming the agent that asked, or omit it.
peerAsk.description: Marks this turn as another agent's ask (`docs/24-SPEC-PEER-ASK.md`): it runs without `handoff` and `ask_agent`, so it is one hop, and the agent is told who asked. It only narrows what the turn may do, so any caller may set it; the control plane's relay always does.

images.hint: Send images as [{ "path": "files/…/shot.png" }] (relative to the agent's directory), or [{ "data": "<base64>", "mediaType": "image/png" }].
images.description: Images sent with this message: PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP, at most five, 3.75 MB each. A path inside the agent's directory, or inline base64 (within the 1 MB body limit). The model receives them on this turn; history keeps an `[image: <path>]` line.

deliver.hint: A bare channel id is not enough on an API turn: the request has no originating conversation, so there is no recipient to infer. Send { "channel": "tg", "to": "12345" }, or "none" to read the reply from the event stream.
deliver.description: Where the reply goes. "none" leaves it on the event stream and in the store.

id.hint: Send { "from": { "id": "agent:ops-bot", "kind": "agent" } }, or omit it entirely for a turn the token-holder is sending itself.
id.description: Stable identifier for the sender. Appears on the turn row and in events.

kind.hint: This field decides the trust boundary — "agent" fences the message and blocks mutating tools for the turn, "user" does not — so there is no default and an unknown value is refused rather than guessed at. A turn the token-holder is sending itself omits "from".
kind.description: The trust boundary. "agent" fences the text as data and blocks mutating tools for the whole turn.

name.hint: A display name, shown beside the sender id. Omit it rather than sending an empty string.

from.description: Attribution for a turn somebody other than the token-holder is sending. Omit for your own.

stream.description: Stream the turn's events inline as SSE rather than returning a handle.

chunks.description: Include per-token `model.chunk` frames. Off by default — the reader decides.

children.description: Include the events of subagents this turn runs (they carry `parentTurnId`). Off by default.

label.description: How this credential is shown in a listing. Required; see `keyLabelProblem`.

scope.hint: Send { "scope": { "agents": ["milo"], "can": ["chat"] } }, or omit it entirely for a key that reaches everything — which is what every key minted before scopes existed does.
scope.description: Opt-in narrowing. Absent is an unscoped key.

agents.hint: Send { "agents": ["milo"] } — a list of agent ids. Omit it for a key that reaches every agent. An id naming no agent on this server is reported rather than silently matching nothing.
agents.description: Agent ids this key may reach. Absent means all of them.

sessions.hint: Send { "sessions": "team_42:" } — a session-key prefix, with an optional trailing "*". A prefix rather than a list, because the conversations this key will cover do not exist yet when it is minted.
sessions.description: Session-key prefix. Absent means every session.

can.hint: Send { "can": ["chat", "read"] }. read (every GET), chat (send a message, answer an approval, stop a turn), write (schedules, phase, clearing a session), admin (keys, provisioning, start/stop/reload), and peer (a plugin route that asks for it — an A2A endpoint — and nothing else). Absent means all five; an empty array means none, and is honoured as written.
can.description: Capabilities this key may exercise. Absent means all of them.

participant.hint: Send { "participant": "user:018f…" } — the id this key speaks for. Every turn it starts acts for that participant: a from naming anyone else is refused, and an omitted one is filled in. Omit it for a backend that names senders itself.
participant.description: The participant every turn this key starts acts for. Absent: any sender.

expiresIn.hint: Send { "expiresIn": 3600 } — whole seconds from now, as a number. Relative rather than an absolute instant, because that would need the caller and this server to agree about the clock; the response reports the absolute expiresAt this server computed.
expiresIn.description: Seconds until this key stops authenticating. Absent means never.

remove.description: Take the field out of the manifest instead of setting it, so it returns to its default. Checked like any edit: a required field is refused. A field that is not there is left as it is. Not sent together with `value`.

confirm.description: Required only for a field whose own row carries a `confirm` sentence. Absent is not consent.

changes.description: Several changes, each `{path, value}` or `{path, remove: true}`, applied in order and checked against the file as the earlier ones left it. One write and one reload; any refusal writes nothing. Sent instead of a top-level `path`.

path.hint: GET /v1/agents/:id/config lists every field this surface may change, with what each one does.
path.description: A dotted path, exactly as it appears in the manifest — `tools.pinned`, `model.main.id`.

value.hint: Text, the way it is typed at a terminal: a bare word, a number, true or false, a list as ["a", "b"], or a map as {k: v}. Quote anything containing a colon or a "#". To take a field out, send { "remove": true } instead.
value.description: The new value, as text. Read by the same parser the `config` command uses. Required unless `remove` is true.
